system.name: Dilu
system.one_liner: a cross-layer, GPU-based serverless DL serving system that supports fine-grained, adaptive two-dimensional GPU resourcing-on-demand

components.name: Profiler
components.role: acquires resource plans for DL functions via pruning-search trials, producing resourcing metadata

components.name: Metadata
components.role: per-function resource plan data (type, SMR, MS, IBS, ...) produced by the Profiler

components.name: Gateway
components.role: receives deployed functions and dispatches requests to target modules

components.name: Workload Monitor
components.role: monitors incoming request workload inside the Gateway

components.name: Load Balancer
components.role: balances dispatched requests inside the Gateway

components.name: Scheduler
components.role: manages instance deployment requirements of DL tasks

components.name: Affinity-First Collocation
components.role: scheduling principle collocating functions by affinity

components.name: Defragmentation Collocation
components.role: scheduling principle collocating functions to reduce GPU fragmentation

components.name: Global Scaler
components.role: informs the scheduler to horizontally scale DL functions (launch/terminate instances)

components.name: Local Scaler
components.role: distributed per-GPU-server component that vertically resizes SM quotas for functions

components.name: Function Instances
components.role: running instances of DL functions serving dispatched requests

components.name: GPUs
components.role: shared GPU hardware on each cluster node hosting collocated function instances

components.name: Cluster
components.role: set of nodes (Node-1, Node-2, Node-n) hosting GPUs and function instances

flows.what: submitted DL function program with QoS description

content.key_idea: Dilu splits into a Control Plane (profiling, gateway, scheduling), a Scaling Plane (adaptive 2D co-scaling via a global and per-server local scalers), and a Serving Plane (collocated function instances on shared GPUs across cluster nodes).
content.reading_order: Top-down and numbered: Developer/User actions at top (submit, deploy, invoke) flow down through the Control Plane, into the Scaling Plane's global/local scalers, and finally into the Serving Plane's function instances on GPUs across cluster nodes.

evidence: The system architecture is depicted in Figure 3. It consists of a control plane, a scaling plane, and a serving plane.
Users submit DL function programs with pre-defined QoS descriptions to the system
The global scaler informs the scheduler to carry out horizontal scaling of DL functions, including launching and terminating instances

summary: This figure shows Dilu's three-plane system architecture for GPU resourcing-on-demand in serverless deep learning serving. In the Control Plane, a Developer submits a DL function with QoS descriptions to the Profiler (step 1), which produces resourcing metadata, and deploys it to the Gateway (step 2), which forwards it to the Scheduler; the Scheduler applies affinity-first and defragmentation collocation principles to launch or terminate instances via the Global Scaler (step 3). When a User invokes a function (step 4), the Gateway's Workload Monitor and Load Balancer dispatch the request (step 5) toward the Scaling Plane, where a Global Scaler coordinates with per-server Local Scalers in an adaptive 2D co-scaling loop (horizontal launch/terminate plus vertical SM-quota resizing). The Serving Plane at the bottom shows the resulting Function Instances collocated on shared GPUs across cluster nodes (Node-1, Node-2, Node-n). Numbered dashed arrows narrate the five-step control flow, while a red dashed line traces the invoke request down to an actual instance.
summary_zh: 该图展示 Dilu 的三层架构：控制平面（Profiler、Gateway、Scheduler）负责提交部署与调度，扩缩平面（Global Scaler 与各服务器 Local Scaler）执行自适应二维协同扩缩，服务平面在共享 GPU 上运行各节点的函数实例，编号箭头串联起完整请求流程。
